requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
requirements.summary: Init script /etc/init.d/inventory-api was created, enabled via rc-update add default, and shown as 'started' both before and after a full node reboot (auto-started on boot), with health/inventory endpoints responding.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api is protected from the kernel OOM killer
requirements.summary: A start_post hook sets oom_score_adj=-1000 on the service pid; verified directly via /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj immediately after start and again just before the OOM event, and independently confirmed inside the kernel's own OOM task dump (pid 3273, oom_score_adj:-1000).

requirements.requirement: A memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory and is the process the kernel stops
requirements.summary: hog.py (pid 3438, oom_score_adj:0) was launched under setsid, consumed memory until free/available memory collapsed, and the kernel's global OOM killer log explicitly shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 3438 (python3)... oom_score_adj:0' — a single, clearly identified victim matching the hog, not inventory-api.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving through the OOM event
requirements.summary: Immediately after the hog was killed, inventory-api's original pid (3273) was still present in the same OOM task dump, and a curl to /health during the same command returned 200 with the same pid and a monotonically increasing uptime value, indicating no restart or interruption occurred.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/OOM/data state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (7045e228...) and healthy service state were captured, the reboot command was acknowledged before the connection dropped, the post-restart boot_id (1a5c0035...) differs and matches the fixed after-executor snapshot, and after reconnecting the service had auto-started under a new pid with oom_score_adj reapplied and both endpoints responding correctly.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: inventory-api is a properly enabled and auto-starting OpenRC service, is hardened against the OOM killer via oom_score_adj=-1000, a genuine memory-hog process drove the node into a real kernel OOM event and was the sole process killed (confirmed in the kernel's own oom-kill log), and inventory-api continued serving uninterrupted with the same pid throughout. The independent mandatory restart protocol is also fully and consistently evidenced, with boot-identity change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: No evidence was captured of memory pressure ramping incrementally (e.g., intermediate free-memory samples) beyond the single dmesg-based confirmation, though the dmesg OOM dump itself is authoritative for the kill event.
Leftover temporary files and the /opt/mem-hog test tool were not cleaned up after the demonstration, though this is low-risk and not explicitly required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were necessary and purposeful: python3 install, service/user/app creation, a corrective fix for a log-permission failure that initially left the service crashed, hog tool creation, the OOM-inducing hog launch, and the mandated reboot. One troubleshooting mutation was not clearly necessary: an early hog launch via plain `nohup ... &` (cmd-5d12207df7d54add) spawned a process that self-terminated when the exec session ended rather than surviving as intended, before the executor corrected the approach with `setsid` in cmd-fc4bc82b0d744835 — a bounded, low-risk failed attempt that left no lasting residue. Several temporary log/pid files (/tmp/apk-install.log, /tmp/dmesg-pre.log, /tmp/hog.log, /tmp/hog.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) and the /opt/mem-hog test tool were left on disk after the task rather than cleaned up; these are low-risk residue but were not restored to the pre-task state.
